2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Payments Technology finalists include Nayax, Sticky and Zyntrix
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Payments Technology category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 Payments Technology finalists as follows:
Croissant Pay
Croissant Pay is a customer wallet and payment method for luxury e-commerce. Shoppers earn Croissant credit through purchases, brand funded credit drops, and resale, then spend it as one balance at any participating merchant's checkout.
Ecommpay
In a market where a failed transaction is lost revenue, and potentially a lost customer, Ecommpay has made its mission to push checkout performance to its absolute limit. A company wide investment in AI is analysing payment declines to transform e-commerce performance.
Edenred Payment Solutions and New Look
New Look transformed the returns experience by introducing a refund to gift card solution, giving customers a faster, more flexible alternative to waiting three to five working days for refunds to reach their bank account
Hozah AutoPay
Hozah AutoPay is a barrier free, ANPR driven payment platform that automatically charges drivers for parking on exit, with no app, ticket, or machine required.
Justt and Madison Reed
Madison Reed, a hair colour brand selling through subscription memberships, direct e-commerce and nearly 100 Hair Colour Bars across the United States, has improved its chargeback win rate by 49% and its chargeback recovery rate by 69% with no increase in customer support headcount.
Nayax
Tigapo by Nayax is a cloud native cashless payment and experience platform built specifically for arcades and family entertainment centres, replacing coin, card and paper ticket systems with one connected ecosystem covering payments, loyalty, redemption and real-time analytics.
Sticky
Sticky is laying claim to a new model for digital hospitality ordering in stadiums: fast, contactless and so simple it can be deployed at any scale. Using NFC contactless touchpoints and a drag-and-drop no-code platform, guests can order in under ten seconds with no app, login or table selection.
Zyntrix
Open Banking has existed for years, but nobody gave retailers or shoppers a reason to use it. Zyntrix's Payments with Purpose changes that.
Retailers enjoy reduced merchant fees by up to 45% and get paid up to 36 hours faster, with their own brand at the heart of checkout. Shoppers pay from their bank with Face ID, earn rewards, and see the saving fund causes they care about. Integrated into existing PoS systems, Zyntrix is live across retail, sport, care and hospitality.
Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

In a LinkedIn post, Patrick Gretsch, Retail Operations Expert at Jysk, said: "Two more countries have taken their first steps towards a new way of working, with the first stores in the UK and Ireland now successfully running on our unified commerce platform."
"I had the pleasure of joining the team at our Sallynoggin store in Ireland to experience one of these first transitions firsthand. What stood out was the excellent preparation and collaboration across all departments involved. The result? A smooth and efficient changeover, completed while the store remained open and continued serving customers."
He added: "And this is just the beginning. The roll-out is progressing at pace, with all Jysk stores in both countries expected to be running on the new platform by mid-November. So, what does this mean for our colleagues and customers? For our store teams, unified commerce means simpler processes and new opportunities to serve customers directly on the shop floor. With mobile PoS, colleagues can process payments right where the customer interaction takes place, making the shopping experience more convenient and personal."
"For our customers, it opens the door to additional services. They can, for example, order products in a store and have them delivered directly coming from our warehouse straight to their doorstep. This is what makes unified commerce so exciting: it’s not just about introducing a new platform. It’s about improving the way we work and creating new opportunities to serve our customers."

The first step in a much bigger journey as Frasers Group switches on first D365 WMS warehouse
Frasers Group, whose brands include Sports Direct, House of Fraser, and Flannels, reports that Antrim in Northern Ireland has become the first of its warehouses to go live with a Microsoft Dynamics 365 warehouse management system (WMS).
In a LinkedIn post, Jakob Vestergaard, Product Manager - Warehouse at Frasers Group, said: "Two years of work. One major milestone. We're live. As the first warehouse in the group to adopt D365 WMS, Antrim marks an important milestone in our wider warehouse transformation journey."

items.body:
Currys hits TikTok Shop and Sainsbury’s launches SmartLists: last week’s biggest retail technology plays
RTIH rounds up the stand out retail technology deals, launches, deployments and pilots from the past seven days. Including VenHub Global, Asda, Rokt, The Very Group, Made With Intent, VoCoVo, Cotswold Outdoor Group, Wayfair, Klarna, Zalando, gorjana, Walmart, Wing, Panda Retail, Deliveroo, and Sur la table.
Sainsbury's
Sainsbury’s has launched SmartLists, a new AI powered feature in the retailer's app that helps customers plan their shop, create a shopping list, find products more easily in-store and manage their budget with Nectar Prices.
Ben Edge, Director of Product at Sainsbury’s, says: “We know our customers are busy and want shopping to feel simple, joyful and easy to fit around their lives. SmartLists is designed to take the effort out of creating and buying a shopping list, whether customers are typing, speaking or taking a picture of what they need."
“Alongside this, by bringing more of our services together in one app, we’re making it easier for customers to plan their shop, build their basket and find products in-store, however and whenever they choose to shop with us.”
Sur la table
Sur la table is joining the Uber Eats marketplace, making its assortment of kitchenware available for on demand or scheduled delivery. The partnership will roll-out to all its locations across the US.
“Our customers trust us to know what works in the kitchen,” says Dan Goldman, President at Sur la table. “Uber Eats lets us bring that same trusted assortment to the moments when cooks need it right now. It's a natural extension of our mission to create and spread joy through cooking, wherever and whenever cooking happens.”
“Customers are increasingly turning to Uber Eats for more than meals, and Sur la table brings an elevated assortment of kitchen essentials to our growing retail marketplace,” says Nathan Bernheim, Head of Retail Partnerships at Uber. “As the holiday season approaches, we’re making it easier to find everything from a last minute host gift to the right appliance for a new recipe, all with the convenience of on demand delivery.”
VenHub Global
VenHub Global has announced plans for the first deployment of its smart store autonomous retail platform at Penn Lofts, a new 59-unit multifamily development in Bend, Oregon, USA. It says that this represents an important expansion of its technology into the multifamily residential market, where it reports growing demand from developers and property owners seeking new ways to enhance the resident experience and differentiate their communities.
“Multifamily residential communities represent a significant growth opportunity for VenHub, and we are seeing increasing demand from developers and property owners who recognise the value of bringing autonomous retail directly into their communities,” says Shahan Ohanessian, Founder and CEO at VenHub.
“Residents increasingly expect convenience to be built into where they live. Our flexible platform helps owners meet that expectation with a distinctive, highly visible amenity that adds value for residents and helps properties stand out - from smaller communities to larger multifamily developments. Penn Lofts is an ideal first deployment to demonstrate how our technology can be thoughtfully integrated into a community from the beginning.”
Asda
Asda has partnered with Rokt to deliver relevant offers to the UK grocery retailer’s customers at checkout across its online grocery business and George, its clothing and home brand. Using Rokt Pay+ on the payment page and Rokt Thanks on the order confirmation page, Asda says it has created a new retail media revenue stream at the point of purchase, while customer conversion remains unchanged.
Rokt uses AI to determine the most relevant next action for each customer in real-time on both the payments and confirmation pages.
“Checkout is a critical part of the customer journey, so we were deliberate about how we approached it,” says Chris Chalmers, Vice President Customer Data and Loyalty at Asda “The results show we can make that experience more relevant for customers while creating meaningful new value for the business.”
Panda Retail
Panda Retail, a grocery retailer in Saudi Arabia, has partnered with Spike Media Saudi, GoWit’s partner in the region, operating locally as GoSpike, to accelerate its digital media transformation push in the Kingdom.
With more than 200 stores, over 14 million online shoppers, and one million monthly active app visits, Panda offers advertisers touchpoints across both physical and digital channels. Building on this reach, the partnership will enable it to expand advertiser participation, manage growing campaign and inventory volumes, and scale its e-commerce media business through more automated, data driven, and measurable media operations.
“As we continue our digital transformation, e-commerce media gives us new opportunities to connect brands with our customers in relevant and measurable ways,” says Ahmad Chehade, CMO at Panda Retail. “Our partnership with Spike Media brings strong Saudi market expertise and advertising capabilities to support the continued growth of our digital ecosystem.”
VoCoVo
VoCoVo has announced the launch of its audio accessibility toolkit and new headset accessories, with a view to bringing inclusive audio solutions and personalised customisation to retail environments. The company says it is offering multiple user led communication solutions to connect its hardware with personal hearing technology.
This is alongside a collection of ergonomic and adaptive accessories that enable teams to personalise their headset for maximum comfort and usability. The solutions have been designed to create a more inclusive working environment while supporting colleague morale.
The Audio Accessibility Toolkit, designed to support retail colleagues with hearing impairments, includes direct integration between the VoCoVo Series 5 (S5) Headset and telecoil enabled hearing devices, requiring no additional hardware installation.
The toolkit also features an ear cushion for behind the ear hearing aids, which funnels sound directly from the S5 Headset into the hearing device, and a handset, offering Bluetooth connectivity for additional flexibility via loudspeaker, earpieces and push to talk communication. Hearing impaired colleagues will be able to process speech more effectively in busy retail spaces with fast changing background noise and during long shifts.
SIMKHAI
Croissant, a shopping and rewards app for luxury fashion, reports that its Croissant Pay solution is now available in Shopify Checkout and at the register through Shopify POS and all other PoS systems. Fashion brand SIMKHAI is among the first to offer it through the new integration.
“Reaching a luxury customer costs more every year, and the first order rarely pays for itself. The industry needs two things: alternative means of acquiring the right shoppers, and deeper loyalty,” says John Howard, CEO and Co-Founder at Croissant.
“Croissant brings both. Our members hold spending power in Croissant: credit from the pieces they've sold, rewards from the brands they shop, and exclusive offers from the brands they want next. Croissant Pay brings that spending power to a brand's checkout and its stores, and the brand pays only when a member spends. Shoppers earn more credit on each subsequent purchase, keeping them loyal to the curated list of brands in Croissant’s network.”
SIMKHAI, a Los Angeles-based fashion house founded by Jonathan Simkhai, began accepting Croissant Pay online on 11th September, the day of its Spring/Summer 2027 runway show, and in its SoHo store on Mercer Street, where it hosted a correlating private shopping event. More than 6,600 Croissant members currently own SIMKHAI items.
“We’re continually exploring thoughtful ways to enhance the SIMKHAI customer experience,” says Martin Vestre, Chief DTC Officer at SIMKHAI. “Croissant Pay offers another way to engage with the brand while introducing SIMKHAI to a new audience.”
“Innovation has always been central to SIMKHAI, both in our design ethos and in how we connect with our customers,” adds Jonathan Simkhai. “Croissant offers a fresh way to discover us, and we’re excited to bring this partnership to our community.”
MAAP
Cycling apparel brand MAAP is adopting Bamboo Rose TotalPLM end-to-end to support its next phase of global growth. By bringing planning, design, product development, sourcing, and order management together on a single AI native platform, it says it will give its teams a single connected source of truth from concept to production.
As MAAP expanded globally, key workflows remained spread across multiple systems. A single product change required updates across three software platforms and multiple spreadsheets, creating unnecessary manual work, limiting visibility, and slowing collaboration across teams.
With TotalPLM, MAAP says it is replacing disconnected workflows with a unified platform that improves data accuracy, increases visibility, reduces manual work, and enables faster, more informed decisions as the business grows.
"Moving to TotalPLM gives our teams a single source of truth across the product lifecycle. We gain the visibility, accuracy, and automation needed to support MAAP's next phase of growth while giving our teams more time to focus on product innovation," says Erin Height, Chief Product Officer and Project Champion at MAAP.
Sereact, Zalando and CEVA Logistics
Sereact, Zalando and CEVA Logistics have announced the launch of AI powered automated returns processing across key fulfillment facilities in Germany (Greven) and Poland (Świebodzin). Powered by Cortex, Sereact’s physical AI platform, the dual-arm robotic systems have entered live operations to autonomously process returned fashion items, marking the initial phase of a broader initiative to scale returns automation across Europe.
Cortex groups previously unseen objects - identifying, grasping and sorting items dynamically without requiring article specific training or pre-determined article sets. The technology is designed to work alongside humans. By taking on highly repetitive handling, it aims to reduce physical strain on employees, allowing them to move into higher value roles where human expertise and judgement are required.
“At the heart of our collaboration with Sereact and CEVA is a fundamental belief: true innovation happens when technology and human potential advance together. By solving the most complex challenges in modern fulfilment today, we are actively shaping the future of e-commerce logistics for fashion and lifestyle,” says Masood Choudhry, SVP Logistics at Zalando, which in July joined Sereact’s Series B round as an investor.
Tata Consumer Products GB
THG Ingenuity has been selected as the strategic e-commerce partner in the UK for Tata Consumer Products GB and its tea and wellness brands teapigs, Good Earth and Organic India.
The tie up will involve: THG Commerce will design, build, and host branded direct-to-consumer websites with a view to providing an intuitive, engaging shopping experience for consumers. THG Fulfil will manage end-to-end fulfilment and customer service operations, ensuring a reliable, efficient delivery experience for retail consumers and trade partners alike. And THG Studios will provide dedicated creative services to support the brands’ digital marketing.
Darren Rajanah, Chief Revenue Officer, THG Ingenuity, says: “We are proud to have been appointed by Tata Consumer Products GB. The collaboration is a true end-to-end partnership, bringing together our integrated commerce, fulfilment, and creative capabilities to deliver an exceptional, seamless experience for their consumers. We look forward to working closely with the Tata team to support their long-term growth ambitions.”
Mat Bird, Marketing Director at Tata Consumer Products GB, comments: "Our brands have been built on quality, trust and strong connections with consumers. Whether consumers discover our brands through retailers or engage with us directly online, it is important that every interaction reflects the high standards our brands are known for. This appointment will help us strengthen the direct-to-consumer experience for teapigs, Good Earth and Organic India, complementing the excellent experience consumers receive through our valued retail partners while supporting the continued growth of our brands."
Wayfair
Klarna has announced an expanded partnership with Wayfair, bringing new payment options to US and Canadian consumers. Eligible US customers can now access always on 0% APR financing up to six months across Wayfair's full family of brands - Wayfair, Joss & Main, AllModern, and Birch Lane.
For Canadian shoppers, it marks the first time Klarna's full suite of buy now pay later options will be available at Wayfair. Across both markets, shoppers can pay in full, split purchases into interest free installments, or finance larger orders over time.
"Wayfair's decision to renew and deepen this partnership speaks to the trust we've built together and the real demand we're seeing for flexible payments for considered home purchases," says David Sykes, Chief Commercial Officer at Klarna. "Home essentials is one of our fastest-growing categories in North America, and having Wayfair's full family of brands behind that momentum is a significant benefit for consumers in both markets."
"Klarna has been a trusted partner in helping our customers shop with confidence, and renewing this relationship was an easy decision," says Curtis Crawford, Director at Wayfair. "Our customers are making meaningful investments in their homes, and giving them flexible, transparent payment options at checkout makes a real difference, and that's exactly what this partnership delivers."
YEEP!
YEEP! reports that it has reached 4,000 parcel locker locations across the UK and is preparing to roll-out its new Generation 3 touchscreen lockers. The company, which operated just over 2,250 locations when Jamie Dickinson was appointed CEO in December last year, is now aiming to reach 5,000 by the end of 2026.
Developed with YEEP!’s hardware partner and shareholder kernTerminal, Generation 3 combines the company’s solar and battery powered technology with a new touchscreen interface designed to significantly improve the experience for both delivery drivers and consumers. All new YEEP! lockers will move to the Generation 3 specification from 2nd November, with a programme to upgrade the existing estate by end of Q1 2027.
Alongside the hardware, a bespoke operating system has been designed around the requirements of an open locker network. The system manages site surveys, installation, scheduling, maintenance and upgrades, with the aim of giving YEEP! greater visibility and control as the network scales.
The Very Group
The Very Group, which operates digital retailers Very and Littlewoods, has partnered with Made With Intent. By using over 800 behavioural signals, Made With Intent’s agentic decision engine predicts customer’s intent in real-time, helping to decide what they see and when.
Very says it will now be able to spotlight discount offers unique to customers based on individual shopping trends, as well as provide prompts at crucial moments throughout the shopping experience. Made With Intent’s engine is built on a proprietary model and optimisation AI agent that work together to allocate experiences across hundreds of intent combinations, learning what works for which visitors and contexts then applying it to future sessions.
Sarah Hanna, Digital Director at The Very Group, comments: “Made With Intent’s agentic platform unlocks fast paced, scalable real-time personalisation that can be executed to help enhance the customer experience, ultimately influencing our commercial KPIs. In fact, in the first month of the partnership, we’ve already seen promising results including revenue per customer increasing by a fifth in one of our agentic strategies, and an uplift in overall conversion.”
“Made With Intent gives our e-commerce team a brand new lever that they can effortlessly activate to make a difference on what our customers see and when, whether that’s one-off discounts or personalised payment options. It’s all about giving customers the right experience at the right time.”
Cotswold Outdoor Group
Broadsign and IUF have announced a collaboration with UK retailer, Cotswold Outdoor Group, to expand its retail media network with an in-store advertising infrastructure. This, according to those involved, provides a unified workflow that streamlines media planning, management, and measurement in-store and across onsite and offsite channels.
The aim is to enable Cotswold’s brand partners to execute omnichannel ad campaigns that engage shoppers at the point of purchase and beyond. The network presently includes 149 till, shelf, totem, large format, and front-of-store displays across 23 stores, which are powered by the Broadsign platform (specifically the Broadsign CMS and Ad Server) and support a range of media.
The platform is helping to streamline operations and centralise content management and network health monitoring. The technology is also advancing screen monetisation opportunities by scheduling ads, automating yield, and balancing complex campaign rules to help Cotswold Outdoor Group capture optimal revenue. Through Broadsign’s integration with Zitcha, Cotswold Outdoor Group’s retail media platform, brand partners, and agencies can extend omnichannel strategies into the physical store environment.
Walmart and Wing
Walmart and Wing have announced the next phase of their US wide network roll-out with plans to bring 30-minute drone delivery to Denver and Seattle metros in 2027, bringing home delivery of thousands of Walmart items to more than 20 major US metros.
To date, the tie up has brought drone delivery access to more than three million customers across major US metropolitan areas, including Dallas-Fort Worth, Atlanta, Houston and Orlando.
“Adding new metros to our expansion speaks to how quickly people across the country are adopting drone delivery," says Heather Rivera, Chief Business Officer at Wing. "We're excited to serve the needs of busy families in nearly 20 major markets spanning diverse communities and climates by delivering the everyday items these families need fast.”
“Expanding drone delivery to Seattle and Denver is about giving more customers a practical option when they need something quickly,” says Greg Cathey, Senior Vice President, eCommerce Transformation, Walmart. “Our stores put everyday items close to the communities we serve, and Wing helps bring those items to customers’ homes in minutes.”
A.F. Blakemore
A.F. Blakemore has expanded its partnership with Snappy Shopper, with more than 70 additional SPAR stores launching on the rapid delivery platform. The roll-out across August and September increased A.F. Blakemore’s Snappy Shopper estate from 95 stores to 167.
Customers in participating areas will be able to order groceries, everyday essentials, snacks, drinks and household products from their local SPAR for rapid delivery through the SPAR Delivered service, powered by Snappy Shopper technology. Around 40 of the new stores are located in areas where Snappy Shopper does not currently have another retail partner.
Jysk
Danish home furnishing retailer Jysk has gone live in Norway with its Enactor powered unified commerce platform. It has spent the last couple of months transitioning all 110 of its stores in the country to the new platform.
This integrates all store systems into one unified solution, with the aim of making everyday processes simpler and more efficient for both colleagues and customers.
“We now have several points of sale throughout the store, which means we can help customers and process payments wherever they are. My team has done an amazing job, and they really love the new way of working. It has been great to see how quickly it has become a natural part of our daily routines,” says Connie Evensen, Store Manager at Jysk Furuset in Oslo.
Sweden and Finland joined the new platform a couple of weeks ago, and the Netherlands and Belgium are up next.
gorjana
invent.ai reports that gorjana has selected its technology with a view to strengthening allocation and replenishment across the jewellery brand’s retail network. gorjana opened its first store in Laguna Beach, California ten years ago and now has nearly 150 locations across the US.
As its retail footprint and assortment have grown, so has the complexity of making sure each store has the right product and inventory for its customers. gorjana says it selected invent.ai to give its planning team greater precision at the store and SKU level, helping the brand understand what is selling where, respond faster to changes in demand and replenish inventory accordingly.
“We’ve grown from one store to nearly 150 in 10 years, and with that growth comes a lot more complexity,” says Andrew Pawling, Chief Operating Officer at gorjana. “Every store has its own customer and demand patterns. invent.ai allows us to get much more precise about the right assortment for each store, so we can use our inventory more efficiently and, most importantly, make sure our customers can find the pieces they’re looking for.”
“gorjana has built a distinctive retail brand by maintaining a strong understanding of its customer as the business has grown,” says Gurhan Kok, Founder and CEO at invent.ai. “We’re pleased to support the next stage of that growth by helping the gorjana team translate customer demand into more precise allocation and replenishment decisions across its expanding store network.”
Deliveroo
Deliveroo is gearing up to roll-out delivery robots, supplied by US company Coco, in the UK. These will be used for takeaways and groceries, with Deliveroo claiming that the robots will not replace human riders but rather complement them during off peak hours.
Canary Wharf, Milton Keynes, Leeds, Stockton-on-Tees, and Nottingham are the initial areas to get the service, with plans afoot for a broader UK roll-out.
Deliveroo runs a three-sided marketplace across roughly restaurants, grocers and retailers, all promising delivery in as little as 30 minutes. It is also a DoorDash subsidiary now, after being taken over by the US giant in a deal valuing the business at £2.9 billion. So this move shouldn’t come as a huge surprise.
Currys
Currys has launched on TikTok Shop with a curated range of products, from health and beauty and coffee to seasonal and audio.
Building on the retailer’s TikTok activity, with its page having bagged over ten million ‘likes’, it will partner with content creators to showcase products to new audiences, and will host TikTok Live shopping events, bringing real-time product demos and instant purchasing to customers' feeds.
This will start as a trial in partnership with THG Commerce who will provide strategy, trading, shop management, weekly live streams and affiliate management services. As an official TikTok Shop partner, THG Commerce says it has generated over £44 million in GMV for its partners by providing a complete solution that covers everything from initial storefront setup and compliance to content creation, global fulfilment and customer services, managed under one roof.
Constructor
Constructor, which powers search and product discovery for retailers including Sephora, The Very Group, Monica Vinader, White Stuff, and Furniture Village, has launched Agentic Checkout, a move that, the company claims, makes it the first to offer Stripe powered checkout directly within an onsite shopping agent.
People on retail sites and apps can discover products, ask questions, get personalised recommendations, and refine their choices, then check out and pay, without leaving the agent experience. They can pay via the Link By Stripe digital wallet or other payment methods.
Agentic Checkout is available within Constructor’s AI Shopping Agent (ASA), which lets shoppers describe what they need in natural language and get guidance based on their context, history and intent, and AI Product Insights Agent (PIA), which answers product specific questions directly on product detail pages. Agentic Checkout will expand to more touchpoints throughout retailers’ digital properties later this year.
“The promise of agentic commerce is that a shopper can express what they need and AI can help them every step of the way, making every part of the journey easier, more helpful, and more enjoyable,” says Eli Finkelshteyn, CEO and Co-founder at Constructor.
“Delivering on that promise requires best-in-class discovery and then best-in-class checkout. Constructor has spent years focused on improving the discovery experience and helping shoppers find the right products, while Stripe has built world class payments infrastructure that helps shoppers buy those products easily and securely. Together, we’re making agentic shopping more complete for consumers and more valuable for retailers.”

items.body:
Tesco Media announces the launch of new ad platform, shoppable formats and smarter in-store media
Tesco Media has unveiled a series of new capabilities designed to help brands turn deeper customer understanding into more helpful media experiences, more connected shopping journeys and clearer proof of growth. These were announced at its 2026 Upfront event.
Key here is Ad Manager, a new client facing platform designed to make planning, booking, measuring and optimising media simpler, more connected and more useful for brands. The self-service platform gives advertisers greater control and transparency over how they work with Tesco Media, while helping them turn customer insight into action with less complexity.
Tesco Media Ad Manager currently delivers Sponsored Products and will expand shortly into Display and Video as Tesco Media builds towards a more unified experience across its media ecosystem. Over time, AI powered workflows and recommendations will help advertisers reduce manual tasks, uncover new opportunities and make faster optimisation decisions, while greater interoperability will allow agencies and brands to connect the platform with the tools they already use.
The aim is to make control feel enabling rather than burdensome, giving brands simpler ways to create media that is timely, relevant and genuinely helpful to customers. The infrastructure behind Ad Manager is powered by Kevel, a specialist provider of API first ad technology for retailers and commerce media networks and designed to help Tesco Media deliver a seamless advertising experience across its digital channels.
Tesco Media is also launching a new influencer proposition, designed to help brands connect creator led inspiration more directly with purchase. With data stating around 40% of shoppers under 45 actively follow influencers for suggestions on good brands and products, the proposition allows approved creator content to appear beyond social platforms in relevant Tesco Media touchpoints. This includes Tesco.com, the Tesco app and digital screens in-store.
Tesco Media will also begin testing shoppable video within search and shoppable display within Favourites, allowing customers to add advertised products directly to their basket. The feature has been developed in response to research showing shoppers highly value this ease of access, as long as it doesn’t disrupt the overall experience.
Following initial trials with brands, Tesco Media will also test new creator led formats across Special Offers and Favourites, aiming to cut the journey from inspiration and discovery to purchase, while keeping the experience useful and relevant for customers.
Tash Whitmey, Managing Director, Tesco Media, says: “Every Little Helps isn’t just Tesco’s retail promise; it’s how we think about media too. We start with the customer and ask how every interaction can be more useful, timely and relevant. These innovations connect what we know about customers with the moments and channels where brands can make a difference, from Tesco Media Ad Manager to creator content to smarter in-store experiences. Leveraging the unique customer insight and reach of Tesco, ultimately everything comes back to the same goal: making media more useful for customers and more effective for brands.”
Tesco Media is also launching Intelligent Store Orchestration. Powered by Barrows Connected Store technology, the capability enables a single campaign to adapt according to real-world context, including store location, time of day, product availability, promotions, weather and local events. The technology has been trialled by a number of brands, including Costa. Its campaign ran across Tesco Express stores in January, resulting in a 47% uplift amongst customers that were new to the product, with brand repeat rate across all customers reaching 29%.
Stacy Gratz, Revenue and Growth Director, Tesco Media, says: “The physical store remains one of the most powerful environments in retail media because context changes constantly. What is useful to a customer at 8am can be completely different at lunchtime or on the way home from work. Bringing greater intelligence into how campaigns respond to those moments allows brands to be much more relevant without making activation more complicated.”
Tesco Media also announced further investment in measurement as it looks to help advertisers understand not only whether campaigns worked, but why. Over the next six months, it plans to expand incrementality measurement across Display, Video, Sponsored Products, Scan as you Shop and Meta, enabling deeper insights across 93% of Tesco Media spend.
It has also developed a new multi-channel geo-lift testing solution to help advertisers understand how media channels work together, including their combined impact on reach, frequency, conversion and incremental uplift. Further work will focus on making full funnel brand measurement faster and more scalable, alongside improving the Tesco Media insights available for advertisers’ own marketing mix modelling.
To streamline the process for brands, it is developing AI powered conversational audience recommendations designed to make those insights faster and easier to activate. Instead of advertisers navigating audience taxonomies themselves, recommendations begin with the objective a brand wants to achieve, reducing audience building time from five to ten minutes per segment to under a minute for multiple segments.
Nick Ashley, Propositions and Go To Market Director, Tesco Media, says: “All these developments are targeted at streamlining the journey for shoppers and brands alike. Customers do not distinguish between “brand” and “performance” journeys: they encounter a series of touchpoints that collectively influence the decision to purchase."
“The opportunity for brands is to use that understanding to make media more helpful - whether that means inspiration, value, reassurance or simply making a decision easier. Our job is to turn the depth of insight Tesco has into something brands can use much more easily in their planning to drive relevance and foster long-term customer loyalty.”

Former Marks and Spencer and Pret A Manger executive Colin Traub gets digital in new challenge at Burberry
Colin Traub has started a new role at Burberry. He comes onboard as its Digital Director, having previously served as Head of Engineering & Integrations at Pret A Manger. His CV also includes stints at M&S and LuxExperience.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: "A big thank you to everyone at Pret for a brilliant last couple of years. It’s been a great first week at Burberry and I’m very excited for this next chapter."
Jon-Paul Brett
Jon-Paul Brett has taken on the role of Chief Digital & Technology Officer at KFC UK & Ireland. He joins from Burberry, where he spent the past ten and a half years, most recently serving as Global Digital Director.
A spokesperson for KFC UK & Ireland said: “Our Original Recipe hasn’t changed. How we run KFC definitely has. Behind the scenes, we’re exploring how AI can empower our restaurants, giving our teams more time to focus on what matters most: our customers and our fried chicken.”
“With 70% of transactions already digital, we’re continuing to modernise our restaurants through new designs, digital kiosks, and digital drive-thrus. Creating a simpler, more convenient experience for customers, whether they eat in or take food to go. So there couldn’t be a better time to welcome Jon-Paul Brett our new Chief Digital & Technology Officer for KFC UK & Ireland.”
They added: “Jon-Paul joined us in July and has wasted no time getting stuck in. He’s been out in restaurants meeting the team members who use our tech every day, while also spending time with our Tech team and franchise partners to understand where the biggest opportunities lie to create best in class experiences for our teams and customers.”
Brett commented: “The best way to understand KFC UK & Ireland is to get close to the restaurants, teams, and franchise partners who bring the brand to life every day. Since joining as Chief Digital & Technology Officer last month, I’ve spent time across the business: meeting restaurant teams, working with our brilliant tech team, and getting to know our franchise community.”
He added: “There’s real energy across KFC; big ambition, passionate people, and a clear opportunity for technology to unlock the next stage of growth. What has stood out most is the pride in the brand, the pace in our restaurants, and the shared desire to keep improving for our customers. KFC UK & Ireland has a bold future ahead, with technology playing a critical role in shaping better experiences for our customers, employees, and franchise partners. Now the focus is on action: building the capability, pace, and partnerships that help our teams, customers, and franchise partners feel the benefit of technology every day.”

items.body:
French retailer JULES taps Ekinops solutions to strengthen web security and support digital usage
JULES, a French menswear retailer with over 350 stores across France and owned by Association Familiale Mulliez, has selected Ekinops solutions as it looks to modernise web security and better support its evolving digital usage.
Based in Roubaix and employing 2,800 people, JULES was looking for a replacement solution capable of providing greater visibility into internet usage, making filtering policies easier to manage and strengthening employee protection against web-based risks, without compromising user experience.
It says it selected Ekinops’ solution for its performance, ease of integration into the existing information system, its ability to facilitate the migration of filtering rules, the quality of website categorisation and the availability of clear dashboards enabling more effective monitoring of usage, blocks and risks. Ekinops’ positioning as a French software provider was also an important criterion, in line with requirements for sovereignty, proximity, GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) compliance and trust in data management.
“With Ekinops SSE (security service edge) solutions, we are choosing a French solution that is closely aligned with our security, compliance, visibility and control requirements across all our employees and sites.” says Michael Lens, Operational Security Manager at JULES
The solution deployed at JULES is built around several complementary components of Ekinops’ cybersecurity portfolio: SWG (Secure Web Gateway), on-premises DNS (Domain Name System) and CASB (Cloud Access Security Broker). The target scope includes headquarters usage as well as store environments. Ekinops teams also supported the upskilling of JULES teams, providing dedicated support, regular follow-up and continuous optimisation from pre-sales through to operations.
“This project illustrates Ekinops’ ability to address the real-world challenges faced by multi-site enterprises: securing web access, simplifying day-to-day operations and delivering immediately actionable operational visibility,” comments Frédéric Napoléone, Cybersecurity Sales Director at Ekinops. “We are proud to support JULES in this initiative with a trusted French solution designed to meet performance and compliance requirements.”

items.body:
Morrisons becomes one of first UK grocery brands to tap autonomous delivery as Just Eat expands trial
Just Eat is expanding its autonomous delivery robot trial with Starship Technologies to Cambourne in Cambridgeshire. This is the first trial location where it doesn't already offer grocery delivery and builds on Sunderland and Milton Keynes deployments.
Morrisons has become one of the first grocery brands to tap the technology, with benefits including adding delivery capacity in the run up to the festive season and during offers such as the regular 'Half Price Wednesdays' on Just Eat. The Cambourne supermarket which is now live is the fourth Morrisons to begin autonomous robot deliveries with three Morrisons Dailys live across Sunderland and Milton Keynes.
Charlotte Exell, Group Online Director at Morrisons, says: “We are pleased to be working with Just Eat and Starship Technologies to trial autonomous robot deliveries from our Cambourne supermarket as we continue exploring innovative ways to serve our local community. Marking our first time offering Just Eat delivery in the area, shoppers ordering from our Cambourne store via the app will have their orders delivered exclusively by robot. In addition to Cambourne, the trial is also underway across three of our Morrisons Daily stores.”
Caroline Bates, Grocery & Retail Director for Just Eat, says: “Our autonomous delivery trials are all about innovating to improve the customer experience - whether that's enabling us to offer delivery in new areas like Cambourne or increase delivery capacity and speeds in the run up to Christmas. We'll be listening closely to customer feedback on this new and exciting service.”
David Ringer, Director of Corporate Accounts in Europe at Starship Technologies, comments: “We're delighted to be serving households across the UK alongside partners as strong as Just Eat and Morrisons. Our smart robots bring advanced autonomous technology to something very ordinary, and they're built for reliability, because their first job is to serve the community and make the grocery shop convenient and fast.”

items.body:
First for THG Commerce as it brings Criteo Sponsored Products to AI Shopping Assistant solution
THG Commerce, part of THG Ingenuity, has integrated Criteo Sponsored Products into its AI Shopping Assistant, built using Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise. THG Commerce says it is the first commerce technology provider in Europe to bring Criteo Sponsored Products into AI powered conversational search, opening up a new retail media opportunity for retailers and brands.
Retailers can now monetise customer conversations through relevant sponsored product placements. The integration places sponsored and organic product recommendations side by side within the same conversation. Brands can reach shoppers in AI driven discovery moments, when intent is high and recommendations are shaped by the shopper's own words. Early results show sponsored products surfaced through the AI Shopping Assistant reached a click-through rate more than five times the average, and a conversion rate more than double the average.
The AI Shopping Assistant draws keywords and filters from each conversation and turns them into tailored product recommendations. When a Criteo Sponsored Product is eligible and relevant, it appears clearly labelled within the assistant's response alongside organic recommendations, adding to the discovery experience rather than interrupting it.
The same relevance models that power Criteo search advertising, including keyword matching, semantic understanding and strict relevance thresholds, apply in the conversational context. Sponsored recommendations appear only when they match what the shopper has asked for.
The integration builds on THG Ingenuity’s broader partnership with Criteo and on its wider collaboration with Google Cloud. THG Commerce has developed a suite of agentic commerce solutions built on Gemini Enterprise. Alongside the AI Shopping Assistant, these include the AI Stylist, which offers AI powered virtual try-on for beauty, apparel and footwear, and Shopping Assistant Insights, which is available in Gemini Enterprise and helps retailers understand what their shoppers want and how the assistant is serving them. Each is delivered as a plug and play SaaS service, available through Google Cloud Marketplace and able to operate independently of the underlying storefront.
Darren Rajanah, Chief Revenue Officer, THG Ingenuity, says: “More and more, customers start their shopping journey with a conversation, describing what they need, the occasion they're shopping for or the problem they want to solve. That is some of the highest-intent traffic a retailer can have, and until now it has largely sat outside retail media. By bringing Criteo Sponsored Products into our AI Shopping Assistant, we're helping retailers monetise those moments using the infrastructure they already have, while making sure every sponsored recommendation is relevant to what the shopper asked for. As with all our AI capabilities, this works as a standalone service that can integrate with any commerce platform.”
Andy Stephen, Managing Director Retail Media UK, Criteo, says: “Shopping discovery is moving beyond the search box, and retail media needs to evolve with it. By bringing Criteo Sponsored Products into THG Commerce’s AI Shopping Assistant, brands can engage shoppers in high intent moments with relevant, clearly labelled recommendations, while retailers retain control of the experience. This integration extends the value of Criteo Sponsored Products into conversational shopping and creates a new opportunity for retailers to monetise AI led product discovery.”
Maureen Costello, VP of UK, Ireland, and Sub-Saharan Africa at Google Cloud says: “Conversational AI is transforming how consumers discover and buy products online. Built on Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise, THG Commerce’s AI Shopping Assistant is setting a new benchmark for agentic retail. By combining our advanced AI capabilities with Criteo’s retail media expertise, THG Commerce is enabling retailers to turn natural shopping conversations into high converting, monetisable discovery moments.”

items.title: Defying retail technology convention, AI looks to slow down the updates and new releases for a while

items.body:
Defying retail technology convention, AI looks to slow down the updates and new releases for a while
In the early days of Silicon Valley, its residents used the phrase “move fast and break things”. Not wanting to wait for public opinion or regulators, the mantra essentially gave a pass to tech companies to develop and release products with impunity, only maybe worrying about the consequences years down the line.
The ethos has helped establish a continual cycle of tech updates and upgrades that has become the tech sector's common state of play in retail. Now, the tech of the moment that’s in the pockets of millions of customers is saying that it’s about time they slowed down a bit.
Steady Improvements and Releases
In any way that tech interacts with the retail and customer space, those that have found something to be popular will work to create the next instalment that’s improved and keeps the momentum going. You can see this at just about every level, including in the world of online gaming.
When you spin Huff N Even More Puff, you’re playing one of what is - at the time of writing - 11 options in the popular game series. The whole collection spans several different takes on the classic story and different gameplay mechanics, with each new release tweaking the formula or adding something new, as this slot did by adding an upgrades mechanic to the hit original game.
Those regular new game releases in the series follow the standardised retail trend in tech of needing to keep the new stuff coming. The most famous showcase of this is with the release cycles of Apple and Samsung, iPhone and Galaxy devices. New flagships are launched each year for annual buyers and to restock the backlog for the future.
While the number of people who upgrade their smartphones every year is relatively small compared to the total market, the brands recognise the need for regular updates and to keep the devices relevant. Incremental developments are still developments, creating the depiction of them being at the forefront of the industry.
Real-World Implications Catch Up to AI
Artificial intelligence apps truly hit the mainstream at the start of 2023, following the late 2022 release of GPT-3.5 by OpenAI. That kicked off a surge of investment into AI companies and rapidly changed the state of play for many businesses seeking to tap into the advertised better-than-human efficiency on offer.
Since then, OpenAI has released 15 new versions of the AI, culminating in the September 2026 roll-out of GPT-6 Astra. Mere weeks into the Astra launch and people lauding its potential, the AI sector decided to very publicly pump the brakes. As reported by The Guardian, OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX AI heads all called for a slowdown.
Calling AI development to date “reckless,” the news has brought about a tremendous wave of scepticism and a sense of it all being too little, too late. With many of these companies eyeing up public offerings and wanting easy excuses, such as public safety, to fill the holes in their books, it’s rumoured that now is the time to cool off for a bit.
So, unlike the status quo shown across retail sectors powered by tech, AI will, seemingly, desert the approach of continuing to pump out newer and better products. Then again, this slowdown is unlikely to last long, given the mindset of Silicon Valley and its ambitions.

items.body:
Grocery giant Morrisons creates Chief AI Officer role: last week's most read retail technology articles
Check out our most clicked retail technology articles from last week, including Constructor, Walmart, OpenAI, commercetools, The Very Group, Made With Intent, Asda, Rokt, Lipstick London, and the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
Constructor claims a first as it launches Agentic Checkout solution powered by Stripe
Constructor, which powers search and product discovery for retailers including Sephora, The Very Group, Monica Vinader, White Stuff, and Furniture Village, has launched Agentic Checkout, a move that, the company claims, makes it the first to offer Stripe powered checkout directly within an onsite shopping agent.
People on retail sites and apps can discover products, ask questions, get personalised recommendations, and refine their choices, then check out and pay, without leaving the agent experience. They can pay via the Link By Stripe digital wallet or other payment methods.
Agentic Checkout is available within Constructor’s AI Shopping Agent (ASA), which lets shoppers describe what they need in natural language and get guidance based on their context, history and intent, and AI Product Insights Agent (PIA), which answers product specific questions directly on product detail pages. Agentic Checkout will expand to more touchpoints throughout retailers’ digital properties later this year.
“The promise of agentic commerce is that a shopper can express what they need and AI can help them every step of the way, making every part of the journey easier, more helpful, and more enjoyable,” says Eli Finkelshteyn, CEO and Co-founder at Constructor.
“Delivering on that promise requires best-in-class discovery and then best-in-class checkout. Constructor has spent years focused on improving the discovery experience and helping shoppers find the right products, while Stripe has built world class payments infrastructure that helps shoppers buy those products easily and securely. Together, we’re making agentic shopping more complete for consumers and more valuable for retailers.”

Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Digital and AI specialist commercetools announces appointment of Katy Hiller as CMO
commercetools has announced the appointment of Katy Hiller as Chief Marketing Officer (CMO). She joins from Unily, where as CMO she led the global function. Previously, Hiller spent seven years at software supply chain company Sonatype, progressing through its marketing leadership to become CMO.
At commercetools, Hiller will lead the company's global marketing strategy, with responsibility for brand, communications, product and field marketing, and demand generation.
“Commerce is entering a period of fundamental change as AI reshapes how consumers shop and how businesses operate,” says Doug McNary, Chief Executive Officer at commercetools. “Katy understands how to turn major shifts in technology into clear market positioning and sustainable growth. She has a proven track record of building high performing global teams and connecting marketing directly to commercial results. That combination will be critical as we take commercetools into its next phase of growth.”
“commercetools has spent more than a decade challenging how enterprise commerce is built, and AI is creating another defining moment for the industry,” says Hiller. “What attracted me to the company is the combination of a strong technology foundation, ambitious customers and a clear point of view on where commerce is going next. My focus will be on turning that into an even stronger global brand and growth engine, and ensuring commercetools leads in this next era of commerce.”
Walmart joins OpenAI's ChatGPT fashion push as Virtual Try On and Favourites launch
A dress spotted on social media, an outfit for an autumn wedding or a new style to try: OpenAI is adding tools to ChatGPT that let shoppers move from an idea to an image of themselves wearing it, with Walmart among the retailers involved from launch.
The new Virtual Try On and Favourites features allow users to visualise clothing and accessories using their own photographs, then save products to return to later. Shoppers can describe what they want, upload an image of an item or use a screenshot as the starting point for a search.
Walmart is bringing its fashion range into the experience. Daniel Danker, EVP AI Acceleration, Product, and Design, said on LinkedIn that the US retail giant was working with OpenAI “from day one” to make its fashion available through Virtual Try On, Shop this Look and Favourites.
The Very Group teams with AI powered e-commerce personalisation platform Made With Intent
The Very Group, which operates digital retailers Very and Littlewoods, has partnered with Made With Intent. By using over 800 behavioural signals, Made With Intent’s agentic decision engine predicts customer’s intent in real-time, helping to decide what they see and when.
Very says it will now be able to spotlight discount offers unique to customers based on individual shopping trends, as well as provide prompts at crucial moments throughout the shopping experience. Made With Intent’s engine is built on a proprietary model and optimisation AI agent that work together to allocate experiences across hundreds of intent combinations, learning what works for which visitors and contexts then applying it to future sessions.
Sarah Hanna, Digital Director at The Very Group, comments: “Made With Intent’s agentic platform unlocks fast paced, scalable real-time personalisation that can be executed to help enhance the customer experience, ultimately influencing our commercial KPIs. In fact, in the first month of the partnership, we’ve already seen promising results including revenue per customer increasing by a fifth in one of our agentic strategies, and an uplift in overall conversion.”
“Made With Intent gives our e-commerce team a brand new lever that they can effortlessly activate to make a difference on what our customers see and when, whether that’s one-off discounts or personalised payment options. It’s all about giving customers the right experience at the right time.”
Morrisons talks embracing opportunities in data and AI as Mohsen Ghasempour joins grocery retailer
Rami Baitiéh, CEO at Morrisons, has taken to social media to discuss the appointment of Mohsen Ghasempour as Chief AI Officer, a newly created role that will see him establish a central data science and AI function for the UK grocery retailer. He joins from Kingfisher, where he had served as Chief AI Officer since March 2024 following more than two years as Group AI Director.
In a LinkedIn post, Baitiéh said: “To keep delivering exceptional value and service, we have to constantly innovate. That's why I am so excited to welcome Mohsen Ghasempour to Morrisons in the newly created role of Chief AI Officer. The creation of this new department reflects our commitment to ensuring we embrace the opportunities in data and AI at pace, with focus, and in the right way.”
He added: “Mohsen is a recognised expert in the field with hands on experience of unlocking the potential of technology to deliver innovative new solutions. Under his leadership, we will put that technology to work where it matters most: driving customer growth, pushing the boundaries of our manufacturing, operational, and commercial excellence, and genuinely empowering our colleagues to deliver measurable business impact.”
He concluded: “Mohsen brings a phenomenal track record, joining us from Kingfisher where he built and scaled their AI operations across Europe under the leadership of my friend, Thierry Garnier. I'm delighted to welcome him to Morrisons, and I'm so glad he could join us on our Leadership Meeting day. Mohsen, a warm welcome to the team!”
Asda and Rokt team up to bring AI powered relevant offers to customers at checkout
Asda has partnered with Rokt to deliver relevant offers to the UK grocery retailer’s customers at checkout across its online grocery business and George, its clothing and home brand. Using Rokt Pay+ on the payment page and Rokt Thanks on the order confirmation page, Asda says it has created a new retail media revenue stream at the point of purchase, while customer conversion remains unchanged.
Rokt uses AI to determine the most relevant next action for each customer in real-time on both the payments and confirmation pages.
“Checkout is a critical part of the customer journey, so we were deliberate about how we approached it,” says Chris Chalmers, Vice President Customer Data and Loyalty at Asda “The results show we can make that experience more relevant for customers while creating meaningful new value for the business.”
Dragons' Den star Touker Suleyman's new beauty brand Lipstick London gets physical at Westfield
Lipstick London, a new beauty brand from Touker Suleyman, Owner and Chairman at Hawes & Curtis and Ghost, has launched a kiosk at Westfield London, White City.
In a LinkedIn post including a photo of himself at the shopping centre, the fashion retail entrepreneur and TV personality, best known for his stint on reality show Dragons’ Den, said: "Here we are this morning (Saturday, 3rd) launching my new brand Lipstick London at Westfield I want to thank everyone queuing up for this new movement. 15 months of hard work has gone into this. Let’s go."

items.title: Retail bosses ramp up pressure on Healey to cut ‘ridiculous’ tax burden
items.summary: The bosses of Marks & Spencer and John Lewis have piled further pressure on the government to slash the “ridiculous” tax burden facing high street firms. Stuart Machin, chief executive of M&S, called on Chancellor John Healey to “restore hope” within the retail industry by turning a corner from Labour’s last two budgets, which he [...]
items.body:
Retail bosses ramp up pressure on Healey to cut ‘ridiculous’ tax burden
The bosses of Marks & Spencer and John Lewis have piled further pressure on the government to slash the “ridiculous” tax burden facing high street firms.
Stuart Machin, chief executive of M&S, called on Chancellor John Healey to “restore hope” within the retail industry by turning a corner from Labour’s last two budgets, which he dubbed a “disaster”.
The strongly-worded intervention, coming less than three weeks before the Budget, will put further pressure on Andy Burnham to deliver on his pledge to rejuvenate Britain’s high streets and town centres.
While the Prime Minister has focussed these efforts on tax breaks for pubs and crackdowns on gambling shops, retailers have warned Burnham that he must help the high street’s biggest operators lead this revival.
Writing in the Daily Mail, Machin said: “I’ve never hidden what I thought of the last two budgets. They were a disaster. Britain needed a plan for growth and got a pile of new taxes and regulations instead. I know money is tight.
“I’m not asking the chancellor to rip up his fiscal rules, but at the very least, he should start unravelling the mistakes of the last two budgets.”
Machin called on Healey to overturn “patently ridiculous” recycling rules, ensure Labour’s workers’ rights crackdown doesn’t “ban the Saturday job” and secure a “common sense” food trade deal with the European Union.
While the Prime Minister has “promised hope again,” the Chancellor must deliver this by “taking the handcuffs off business and putting money back in people’s pockets,” the M&S boss said.
‘Fundamental misunderstanding’ of retail
Jason Tarry, the chairman of John Lewis and Waitrose, added his voice to the number of retail bosses urging Healey not to hike taxes on the biggest high street businesses.
Concern is mounting in the industry that Burnham could fund business rates cuts for pubs by hiking the bills paid by warehouses, which retail bosses say would send their costs spiralling and ultimately push up prices for shoppers.
Writing in the The Telegraph, Tarry said that a so-called “warehouse tax” would “reveal a fundamental misunderstanding of how modern high streets work”.
The John Lewis boss warned that the tax would hit “a far greater number of high street shops than warehouses.
“In our case, the higher charge applies to just 18 distribution centres, but over 200 John Lewis and Waitrose stores.”
Earlier this week, the boss of Tesco urged Healey not to impose the “warehouse tax,” adding that he has told the government to exempt retailers from the highest business rates multiplier.
Ken Murphy, chief executive of the UK’s biggest grocer, said: “We have long argued that the rate system is fundamentally unfair, that retailers pay – on average – four times their fair share of rates.”
The British Retail Consortium (BRC) – which represents grocers like Tesco, Sainsbury’s and Marks & Spencer – has hit out at the “punishing” tax burden facing the industry in recent months.
Retailers pay 72p in tax for every pound they make, according to the BRC’s analysis, which makes it the second-highest taxpaying sector, behind only hospitality.

items.title: M&S boss Stuart Machin: My six ways Healey can get Britain growing again
items.summary: I've never hidden what I thought of the last two Budgets. They were a disaster.
items.body:
M&S boss STUART MACHIN: Here are my six ways Healey can get Britain growing again
I've never hidden what I thought of the last two Budgets. They were a disaster. Britain needed a plan for growth and got a pile of new taxes and regulations instead. At M&S we were left facing £150million of new costs each year, on top of a tax bill of around half a billion pounds.
Attention is now turning to the next Budget, the first by Chancellor John Healey. I have written to him directly to set out what needs to change, and why it can't wait.
Last month the Prime Minister promised Britain 'hope again'. It struck a chord, and you can see why. People want to believe things can get better. But the speech left big questions unanswered, above all what it means for business and the economy in the coming year.
I was glad to hear the Chancellor reference growth 16 times in his conference speech. He said it's 'the only long-term answer'. He's right. Now the Budget must match his words.
Marks & Spencer chief executive Stuart Machin says the Chancellor 'could get Britain growing by taking the handcuffs off business and putting money back in people's pockets'
John Healey's first Budget is in three weeks. Stuart Machin has written to the Chancellor directly
Retail has a big part to play. It's the engine of the everyday economy, employing more than three million people and keeping customers supplied with what they need. But margins are wafer thin. When the Government piles on costs, there is very little room to soak them up.
At M&S, we’re investing over £2billion in the next three years across our stores, supply chain and technology. But every pound that goes on new taxes is a pound we can't invest.
I know money is tight. I'm not asking the Chancellor to rip up his fiscal rules. But at the very least, he should start unravelling the mistakes of the last two Budgets.
So here are six ways John Healey could get Britain growing by taking the handcuffs off business and putting money back in people's pockets. The first three wouldn't even cost the Treasury a penny.
First, scrap the upcoming Deposit Return Scheme – it's patently ridiculous. Next October, you'll pay 20p more for every bottle or can of drink. To get it back, you'll have to lug bags of empties back to the shops – despite already paying your council for collections. And stores need to rip out shelves to make space for monstrous recycling machines. Retailers are spending tens of millions just to set it up, and will pay millions more every single year to run the scheme.
Second, make sure the Employment Rights Act doesn't ban the Saturday job by treating normal weekend shifts as 'low hours' contracts. The Chancellor spoke recently about his first job, washing pots in a pub. Mine was pushing trolleys at 16. With nearly a million young people out of work or training, don't let the small print pull up the ladder.
Stuart Machin with then-chancellor Rachel Reeves and long-serving M&S employee Allison Burnley, centre
Third, get a food and drink deal with the EU over the line. It's common sense. Cut the red tape with our nearest neighbours, so the European food we love costs less to bring in, and our brilliant British farmers can sell more abroad. Every month it's delayed, farmers and shoppers pay the price.
Fourth, undo the most damaging part of the disastrous rise in National Insurance: the cut to the threshold where employers start paying. It hit shops hard, because so many of our jobs are entry-level and part-time, often just a shift or two a week. It also hit our suppliers, particularly in farming and food manufacturing, and strict regulations meant most of those costs ended up with retailers. These pressures were always going to be felt at the till.
Fifth, fix business rates. Retail makes up around 5 per cent of the economy but pays over a fifth of all business rates. That's not sustainable. M&S alone pays around £170million a year. It's right to support the pubs, bars and music venues on high streets that bring our towns to life. But if you do that by taxing supermarkets, you're paying for a cheaper pint by loading costs on to the weekly shop.
Sixth, get rid of the packaging tax. Extended Producer Responsibility was sold as investment in recycling, but it's nothing of the sort. It's a tax of almost £2billion on food and drink, and even the official forecasters at the OBR now treat it as one. In April, M&S had to pay an extra £40million in one go. Scrap it, and shoppers will feel the difference.
The last two Budgets were a crushing disappointment for customers, colleagues and businesses. Now there's a new Chancellor and a new chance. The Prime Minister has promised 'hope again' and given us ideas for the next Parliament. But the Chancellor needs to restore hope among British businesses, and tell us what he’ll do now.

items.title: Stuart Machin of M&S is not sparing Labour's blushes, says ALEX BRUMMER
items.summary: Machin's charge that the last two Budgets 'were a disaster' will not be easy reading for their author Rachel Reeves.
items.body:
Stuart Machin of M&S is not sparing Labour's blushes, says ALEX BRUMMER
Stuart Machin of M&S is not sparing Labour’s blushes ahead of the October 28 Budget with a blistering attack on business taxes.
Even Britain’s low octane financial lobby groups finally have been spurred into action with a passionate plea to spare the banks further tax punishment.
His full-fronted assault on the Government’s tax raids is a refreshing intervention by a retailer who, together with his chairman Archie Norman, is reinventing M&S for the mid-21st Century.
Machin’s charge that the last two Budgets ‘were a disaster’ will not be easy reading for their author Rachel Reeves.
The M&S chief executive backs up his words with figures. Labour already has added £150million to M&S’s annual costs at a company which pays £500million in taxes a year.
The message from Machin will have resonance among voters in seats across the country where M&S is a presence.
The group currently is involved in a big expansion programme with a landmark new store in Liverpool doubtless visited by some Labour faithful during conference.
Stuart Machin of Marks & Spencer is not sparing Labour’s blushes
It is also opening new M&S Food Halls across the country. This includes Norcross, not far from the working people’s stronghold of Blackpool. Machin applauds Andy Burnham’s refreshed message of giving ‘hope again’.
He is still waiting to see the beef ahead of John Healey’s first Budget, demanding the ‘handcuffs’ come off business.
Quite how that will happen, given the fiscal black hole which is likely to open by the end of this Parliament, is questionable.
Burnham is full of ideas but seems incapable of bringing them to fruition.
The frustration over the failure to decide on drilling the Rosebank and Jackdaw North Sea oilfields angers Norway’s Equinor and has given rise to misgivings at Britain’s oil major Shell.
It has big investments in refining, oil trading, and downstream supplies of energy to motorists, the transport industry, business and agriculture.
Despite smoke and mirrors the much-vaunted National Care Service will not start to see the light of day before the next Parliament.
The opportunity to build a care endowment fund, by adopting a German-style social market levy, appears to be beyond the comprehension of this government.
Yet such boldness was precisely part of the thinking behind the creation of the NHS by the much-admired Atlee government, which pressed ahead in the face of a post-war debt to national income ratio of 250 per cent.
It is to Reeves’ credit that as Chancellor she recognised the need to unlock growth by investing in a third runway at Heathrow.
There has been much waffle, since Burnham took office, about Heathrow failing to put in a formal request for a licence. Moreover, the Government’s £49billion plan for a third runway, which would cross the M25, would be hard to deliver.
Much more practical is the plan put forward by the Heathrow Reimagined campaign and spearheaded by one of Britain’s most patriotic entrepreneurs, Surinder Arora, who is responsible for much of the hotel hospitality industry at the airport.
His scheme for a shorter runway, which can accommodate narrow body jets, is sensible, rooted in commerce and can be delivered for £25billion.
US contractors Bechtel, with a proven record of airport developments, could play a big role.
As one of the great entrepot economies, driven by financial and the services economy, as well as smart innovation from the likes of Deep Mind and Revolut, Britain needs the very best transport hub. Burnham needs to grab the joystick.
